reason: Throughout this passage, Moses is unambiguously portrayed as an established national leader of Israel. God explicitly commissions him to lead the Israelites out of Egypt ('וְהוֹצֵא אֶת־ עַמִּי בְנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמִּצְרָֽיִם'), he mediates between God and the people, makes critical decisions (organizing the Passover, distributing manna, managing disputes, conducting warfare against Amalek), receives and communicates divine law, and exercises authority over the entire community. By the passage's end, when Jethro advises him on establishing a judicial system, Moses is already functioning as the supreme leader of the nation. He is not portrayed as aspiring to leadership but as actively exercising it.
